chunk_arm.note: best-matching 4,000-char chunk per gold file -- the unit retrieval actually delivers, where a file's distant prose cannot carry the seat

mechanism: unicode61 splits on non-alphanumerics, so snake_case identifiers index as the words a natural-language query produces. Rewriting them to camelCase collapses each into one opaque token that shares no term with the query; the extractor cannot compensate because it lowercases before it splits.
scope_limits: Measures query-term OVERLAP (reachability), not delivered recall. A term the gold keeps may still be outranked; a term it loses cannot be recovered by any ranking change.

The twin is a mechanical rewrite of the gold only. In a real camelCase repository the surrounding corpus is also camelCase, which changes document frequencies and therefore BM25 weights; this probe holds the rest of the corpus out of scope entirely.
MULocBench queries are filled GitHub issue forms -- long natural language. A corpus queried by pasted identifiers would show a much smaller loss, since exact identifiers match either spelling.
Gold files over 200 KB are skipped; the count is in `skipped`.
